http://www.bignewsnetwork.com/news/27919.text: Big News Network.com Hungarian PM to ask chess grandmaster Judit Polgar to serve as president BUDAPEST, July 19 (Xinhua) -- Hungary's Prime Minister Peter Magyar said on Sunday that he will meet chess grandmaster Judit Polgar on Monday to ask her to serve as the country's new president. In his Facebook post, Magyar described Polgar as a figure "synonymous with talent and perseverance," adding that the country needs "unity, peace, and a president of whom every Hungarian can be proud." He said the presidency represents "the highest form of service," and that he would consider it an honor if Polgar accepted the nomination. Polgar, born in Budapest in 1976, is a Hungarian chess grandmaster and a five-time Chess Olympiad champion. Hungarian President Tamas Sulyok on Saturday signed the country's 17th constitutional amendment, triggering the end of his mandate as head of state. https://jowhar.com/man-detained-after-ma.text: Home NEWS WORLD NEWS ARTICLE POLITICS SPORT Somali TV Quran karim NEWS ARTICLE WORLD NEWS POLITICS Sport QURAN Video Somali TV privacy-policy terms and conditions Home NEWS WORLD NEWS ARTICLE POLITICS SPORT Somali TV Quran karim NEWS WORLD NEWS Facebook X Telegram WhatsApp ReddIt Pinterest Digg Police reportedly received an email ⁠about the threat to Donald Tusk (centre) and Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz (left) (file image) A suspected plot to assassinate Poland’s top leadership has been disrupted after police arrested a man accused of threatening Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, Mr Tusk said. “The man threatening an attack has been detained,” Mr Tusk wrote on X, commending officers for their “swift and decisive action”. The arrest followed an earlier alert from Poland’s interior ministry, after security services called an extraordinary meeting to assess information pointing to a potential attack on ⁠Prime Minister Tusk and Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz. Special services spokesperson Jacek Dobrzynski said he could not provide further details, but stressed that investigators were treating the report as “deadly serious”. “We are talking about a high probability of these threats being carried out,” he told reporters. Interior Ministry spokesperson Karolina Galecka said the State Protection Service — tasked with safeguarding senior officials — had passed an email containing information about the possible attack to police. Private broadcaster Radio Zet also reported that police had received an email warning ⁠about the threat. Police are seen outside the school where a 15-year-old boy fatally stabbed the caretaker Poland records relatively little violent crime compared with many countries, but the political climate remains sharply divided, and the nation has faced heightened security concerns linked to its proximity to the war in Ukraine. In August, police detained a 23-year-old man accused of calling for the assassination ⁠of senior Polish politicians. In 2024, Mr Tusk said he received threats ⁠after an assassination attempt on Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico. The latest development comes as Polish authorities are already operating on heightened alert in the wake of a spate of violence in schools that culminated in the killing of a caretaker on ‌Thursday. Mr Tusk has said the attacks in schools were “spontaneous acts” fuelled by the online “glorification of violence”. Three attacks at schools in Mazovian province in central Poland took place within four days, leaving one person dead and many injured, including children. Police hugging children outside the school where a 15-year-old boy fatally stabbed the caretaker By this morning, police had detained 117 people nationwide for carrying knives or other dangerous weapons, or for making threats to attack schools or fellow students. Officers also checked some 64,000 schools. “We are not dealing with any group organised on a big scale,” Mr Tusk said during a crisis meeting with government and security services. “These are very often spontaneous actions inspired by online activity. “In the past years and months, we have noted – globally and in Poland – a rise in the fascination with violence.” A post on X shows a teenager in a mask in Warsaw ahead of what was called ‘bloody Friday’, which prompted the closure of several schools Mr Tusk said the incidents could be linked to what he called “nihilistic violence” — a term authorities use for attacks motivated by a nihilistic worldview and misanthropy rather than clear political aims. In Poland’s case, he said, “some of the people detained are active in the ultra-right environment”. He added that officials have tracked intensified online searches for Nazi material, as well as interest in “mass killers who have become idols online”. Mr Tusk described the trend as a broader “civilisational phenomenon”, arguing that children can begin with video games — even mundane ones — or true-crime stories and then be drawn into progressively more violent content. https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/11/08/azbe.text: Azbeszttel szennyezett kőzúzalékot találtak a Gyömrői Fekete István Általános Iskola közelében – derült ki az RTL vasárnapi híradójából. A területet lezárták, és geotextillel letakarták. Egy szülő arról beszélt a híradónak, hogy petíciót indítottak, amiben további méréseket követelnek, hogy kiderüljön, a környező telkek is szennyezettek-e. Eddig 50 család írta alá a petíciót. Az iskolának most építenek új épületet , ezt kedden jelentette be Magyar Péter miniszterelnök. Reagált az önkormányzat is, az anyag mielőbbi elszállítását követelik. A területre már megtiltották a belépést az azbesztes kő felfedezése után, mondta Kisberk Szabolcs gyömrői polgármester. A város összesen kilenc helyszínen vett mintát, és csak azon az úton mutatták ki az egészségre meglehetősen ártalmas anyagot, amelyik az iskolához vezet. A mérésekre azért volt szükség, mert a szomszédos Maglódon egy gyömrői cégtől származó kőben találtak azbesztet. Az önkormányzat megkereste az út tavalyi építéséért felelős Magyar Közutat, és megkérték őket, hogy vigyék el a szennyezett anyagot. A Magyar Közút azt ígérte, hogy vizsgálatot végeznek, és ha az is kimutatja az azbeszt jelenlétét, akkor elszállítják. Az önkormányzat azt mondta, ha nem tudnak megegyezni a Magyar Közúttal, akkor saját hatáskörben intézik el az elszállítást – és ennek a több milliós költségét visszaperelnék. Mivel az azbeszt apró rostjai belélegezve hosszú távon súlyosan rákkeltő hatásúak, a probléma megoldásáig szakértői javaslatra geotextíliával fedték le az érintett területet és a porzást locsolással enyhítik. A környéken élők aggódnak a gyerekek egészsége miatt, mert iskola és óvoda is van a közelben, sokan már elkerülik a környéket. Az utakra szórt azbeszt eddig leginkább Magyarország nyugati részén okozott gondokat. A témáról szóló cikkeink itt olvashatóak .
